sentences.text: Herrerasaurus measured about 6 meters in length and weighed approximately 350 kilograms.
Adult individuals reached a total length of up to 6 meters, a skull length of 56 centimeters, and a weight of 350 kilograms.
Smaller specimens of this animal measured approximately 4.5 meters in length and weighed about 200 kilograms.
The outer toes were small, with the first toe possessing a small claw.
The genus Herrerasaurus was first described by Osvaldo Reig in 1963.
The name means "Herrera's lizard" and honors the rancher who found the first specimen in 1958 in South America.
The holotype specimen PVL 2566 was discovered in the Cancha de Bochas Member of the Ischigualasto Formation in San Juan, Argentina.
Herrerasaurus was a carnivore that preyed on small and medium-sized plant eaters based on its teeth and size.
Dental microwear patterns suggest Herrerasaurus may have mainly consumed small prey swallowed whole with minimal oral processing.
Coprolites containing small bones but no plant fragments from the Ischigualasto Formation have been assigned to Herrerasaurus.
Analysis of coprolites suggests that if they belong to Herrerasaurus, the animal could digest bone.
Following the discovery of a nearly complete skeleton in 1988, most phylogenies classify Herrerasaurus as an early saurischian.
Herrerasaurus belongs to the family Herrerasauridae, which includes some of the earliest genera in dinosaur evolution.
Ischisaurus cattoi and Frenguellisaurus ischigualastensis are considered synonyms of Herrerasaurus.
All known fossils of Herrerasaurus come from the Ischigualasto Formation in northwestern Argentina, dating to the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 231.4 million years ago.
Herrerasaurus lived in the Carnian stage of the Late Triassic, approximately 231.4 million years ago, in what is now South America.
There is a persistent scientific debate regarding whether Herrerasaurus is a basal saurischian or a primitive theropod, with different researchers supporting each view.
For many years, the classification of Herrerasaurus was unclear, leading to hypotheses that it was a basal theropod, basal sauropodomorph, basal saurischian, or even a non-dinosaur.
A mix of primitive and derived characteristics confused early researchers regarding the systematic position and phylogenetic relationships of Herrerasaurus.
Paul Sereno argued that Herrerasaurus should be classified as a primitive theropod.
If Herrerasaurus is a theropod, it suggests that theropods, sauropodomorphs, and ornithischians diverged before the middle Carnian and independently evolved features like an advanced ankle joint.
